doc.title: Charles Lloyd — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The tarogato from Hungary and the mysterious gift
summary: Lloyd tells how a Roma musician in Hungary played the tarogato for him, and how two Roma men later left one at his house.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone

blocks.x: The Taragato. I gotta ask you about the Taragato.
I was in Hungary and someone brought - what do you call the Roma people? What do you call the Roma people?

Gypsies! They brought a gypsy guy to my hotel and he played this thing for me - Mehau Dresh is his name. And he played this thing for me. So I fell on the floor and started foamin’ at the mouth and rollin’ around. And he said, “No, it’s our folk instrument. You can’t have one because we don’t let it out of the country.” That kind of thing. It’s a Transylvanian instrument.

So I said, “Alright, cool.” And then one day at our very house here, some Roma people - two guys - came and knocked on the door. They knocked on the door and they had a little box with a Hungarian flag in it, and they had an old taragato that the brought to me. And I was upstairs in the skybox. And when I came down. Honey, can you get me the case? Or is it put away, for the taragato?
Yeah. The original one. So when I came down to thank them, they were gone.
I want to show it to you cause it’s got a little Hungarian flag pinned to the thing, and...
